sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Fulghor, Champion of Nightglow**, also known as the **Darkdrift Knight** and the **Night Centaur**, is a Nightlord boss in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Fulghor was a gallant and pious centaur who, in ancient times, undertook an arduous quest in service of radiant gods that cloaked themselves in thunder. When his left arm was severed from behind, he realized his comrades had betrayed him and the gods they served.

Fulghor later encountered and embraced the Night, but his holy zeal did not falter. He channeled a sacred form of the Night's power and was consumed by battle, becoming a Nightlord and the champion of Nightglow.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Fulghor, Champion of Nightglow is the Nightlord fought on the final night of the Darkdrift Knight Expedition. The Darkdrift Knight is a masked, one-armed centaur with a massive sword. He is a swift, heavy-hitting boss with high mobility. During the second phase, he grows a new left arm.

- Fulghor deals Standard and Holy damage.
- Fulghor's greatest weakness is Lightning damage. If he takes Lightning damage during his power-up move, a lightning bolt strikes him from the sky. This staggers him and prevents him from casting the spell that creates golden spears beneath the players.
- Fulghor is resistant to Holy damage and is fully immune to Madness buildup. He is vulnerable to all other Status Ailments equally: Poison, Rot, Blood Loss, Frostbite, and Sleep.

- Fulghor was the second Everdark Sovereign to debut.
- Among the Nightlords, Fulghor is the only one whose title is not simply just "of Night", rather "of Nightglow".
- During the Everdark fight, Fulghor's glowing cross bears some resemblance to Miquella's Cross.
- Also in his Everdark form, Fulghor is able to air-walk, not unlike Spirits such as Torrent and the Ancestor Spirit.
- Fulghor shares some characteristics with Gundyr from the *Dark Souls* series:
 - Their heavy build, armor, and helmet design.
 - Their transformation with an oversized, left arm of darkness.
 - Their alternate encounter, with both as their non-afflicted selves.

Glintstone Crowns** are a group of Headwear in Elden Ring. They are granted to Glintstone Sorcerers whose pursuits at the Academy of Raya Lucaria were deemed worthy, indicating the conspectus to which they belong. The nine stone masks each resemble the founder of their associated field of study and are set with glintstones of varying color.

sections.heading: Notes

- The Witch's Glintstone Crown variant worn by Sorceress Sellen's second body, which features a larger crystal, is unobtainable.
- Four additional variants are also unobtainable: a Karolos crown with light blue crystals, a Lazuli crown with red crystals, an Olivinus crown with yellow crystals, and a Twinsage crown with purple and magenta crystals.
- Graven Masses are formed from the glintstone crowns of sacrificed scholars.
- Alberich's Pointed Hat and Alberich's Pointed Hat (Altered) feature red glintstones but aren't true glintstone crowns, as Thorn Sorceries are disdained by the Academy.
- Although Sorcerer Thops's pursuits warranted a new conspectus and crown in his image, his contemporaries deemed them unworthy. Consequently, he never received a glintstone crown.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Hoarah Loux, Warrior**, also known as **Godfrey, First Elden Lord** and the **Lord of the Battlefield**, is a mandatory boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Godfrey is a former consort of Queen Marika the Eternal and the first Elden Lord of the Golden Order. Although his actions directly shaped much of the history of the Lands Between, Queen Marika stole his grace and banished him to the badlands.

Both encounters with Godfrey are mandatory boss fights:
1. The first encounter, **Godfrey, First Elden Lord**, is a golden phantom from the past that ambushes the player at Leyndell, Royal Capital. Defeating this Great Enemy boss unlocks the Erdtree Sanctuary Site of Grace and grants a Talisman Pouch and access to Marika's Bedchamber.
1. The second battle is at the Elden Throne in Leyndell, Ashen Capital. The real **Godfrey, First Elden Lord** transforms into **Hoarah Loux, Warrior** during the fight. Defeating this Legend boss grants the Remembrance of Hoarah Loux and access to the Stone Platform inside the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: Lord Godfrey was once known as Hoarah Loux, a simple, yet ferocious warrior with a ceaseless lust for battle. He was an unmatched champion who earned his right to Lordship through sheer strength. Later, he took the name Godfrey when he took the spirit of Serosh upon his back. The Lord of Beasts suppressed his rage,allowing him to conduct himself in a manner befitting Marika's first Elden Lord.

sections.heading: Age of the Erdtree
sections.markdown:
Before it came to be an embodiment of Order, everything was in opposition to the Erdtree. Godfrey led Marika's golden armies in the War Against the Giants, a decisive conflict thay ended with the Giants' defeat and the confinement of the Fell God's Flame of Ruin. This war heralded the birth of the Erdtree, and the beginning of an age of Order ruled over by Marika and her Elden Lord.

The age of the Erdtree began amidst conflict, and Godfrey was regarded as the "Lord of the Battlefield." He fought the Storm Lord alone and emerged the new lord of Stormveil. Later, during the siege of Castle Morne, Godfrey bested a lone hero who wielded a grafted blade and fought for vengeance. Godfrey was commander of the Crucible Knights, and Ordovis and his men honored their master by wearing the crest of the axe, a symbol of Godfrey's.

Godfrey and his offspring with Queen Marika were the first Demigods, known as the Golden Lineage. His bond with Serosh became an emblem of this lineage, guiding them as they conquered the Lands Between. Godfrey's double-headed axe symbolized his warrior's vow of conduct and would later become a symbol of the Golden Lineage.

sections.heading: The Long March
sections.markdown:
At the end of his campaign, Lord Godfrey's golden armies remained unvanquished and unbowed. When his last enemy fell, it was said that the golden hue of Godfrey's eyes faded. He found his Grace lost, tattered, and faded.

Godfrey and his warriors were then informed by Queen Marika that she had divested them of their Grace. She drove them from the Lands Between to wage war in a distant land, where they would live and die. Marika promised Godfrey and his men that after their deaths, they would regain what she had taken from them. They would return to the Lands Between with the strength required to brandish the Elden Ring.

Thus, Godfrey and his kinfolk became the Tarnished. They left the Lands Between together on a pilgrimage known as the Long March, at the end of which Godfrey divested himself of kingship and became a simple warrior once more.

Godfrey became a chieftain of the Badlands under the name of Hoarah Loux. The head of his axe had been broken in a battle fought during the Long March. His loyal warriors honored him by wielding axes of their own, and they became the weapon of choice for Badlands chieftains.

sections.heading: Return to the Lands Between
sections.markdown: At some point, Hoarah Loux died. However, when the Elden Ring was shattered following the death of his son Godwyn the Golden, the Tarnished that died outside the Lands Between were returned to life by the call of their long-lost Grace. The Tarnished, who had grown strong in the face of death, crossed the fog and returned to the Lands Between, to stand before the Elden Ring and become Elden Lord. Godfrey was among those who made their way back to the Lands Between.

sections.heading: The Ashen Capital
sections.markdown:
After the Tarnished champion has claimed the Great Runes, burned the Erdtree, and unbound the Rune of Death, they return to the city of Leyndell and approach the Erdtree. At the Elden Throne, they find Godfrey, Serosh on his back, mourning the death of his son Morgott, whom the Tarnished had previously slain.

Godfrey rises to his feet and addresses the Tarnished. He acknowledges their effort; however, he declares his intention to seek an audience once again. The two Tarnished do battle, and Godfrey finds himself overpowered. The former Elden Lord grabs the head of Serosh, thanks him for his service, and then tears him from his back. Drenched in the blood of his loyal regent, Godfrey resumes the fight, now as the savage Hoarah Loux. Nevertheless, the Tarnished defeats Hoarah Loux, who declares that their strength befits a crown.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.markdown: This is a boss fight against a golden, spectral version of Godfrey. He is fought within the Erdtree Sanctuary, accessed by climbing up a large root south of the West Capital Rampart Site of Grace. This battle is **not** optional as he must be defeated to progress Leyndell further and continue the story. Compared to the later encounter, this version of Godfrey has a greatly reduced moveset, mainly consisting of close-range axe swings. He can create areas of effect by stomping or smashing his axe into the ground, and he may also throw his axe at the player from a distance.

sections.heading: Environment
sections.markdown: Godfrey is fought in a long, fairly spacious room. There is a narrower, lower section to the left of the entrance, as well as various pillars which may restrict movement or allow one to gain distance from the boss.

sections.heading: Leyndell, Ashen Capital
sections.markdown: Nepheli Loux, Warrior and Shabriri are both available as summons for this fight, provided their questlines have been completed. Like the first battle, this fight is **not** optional and must be defeated to reach the final bosses of the game.

sections.heading: Phase 1 - Godfrey, First Elden Lord
sections.markdown:
Godfrey will usually initiate the fight by throwing his axe at the player and then dashing after it.

Godfrey has a stomp attack similar to that of the Crucible Knights, causing spikes to come out of the ground that are easier to dodge by jumping than to i-frame with a roll. He will generally follow up on the spike stomp with a series of axe swings, but can do a second stomp at any time, even repeatedly.

Godfrey's primary offense will be axe swing combos. They can be dodge rolled safely and involve enough delays for the player to sneak in a hit before having to dodge again.

He retains his moves from the earlier fight, with the addition of more close-range axe attacks and some abilities that generate earthquakes.

sections.heading: Phase 2 - Hoarah Loux, Warrior
sections.markdown:
After his health drops below 50%, a cutscene plays and phase 2 begins. Godfrey no longer has Serosh or his axe, and has an almost entirely new, grappling-based fighting style.

Phase 2 always starts with him rushing towards the player with a delayed command grab. He will always briefly go into slow-motion mid-jump, which can roll-catch. He will attempt to grab the player like this multiple times over the course of phase 2. Properly rolling out of the way of it gives you one of the largest time windows to attack him out of his entire phase 2.

He will do many other grab attacks, ground-slams, leap attacks, delayed kicks and delayed stomp attacks. Panic-rolling and blocking is not recommended.

When he begins to crack the ground after a leap attack by smashing his hands into the ground, the player must run away from him as far as they can, otherwise they will get blown up by an explosion that is very difficult to roll through. He often announces this attack by knocking the player away from him with a roar.

sections.heading: Environment
sections.markdown: The arena is a wide, circular platform with no obstacles. It is the same arena where Morgott, the Omen King was fought previously.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Defeating the golden **Godfrey, First Elden Lord** at Leyndell, Royal Capital for the first time unlocks the "Godfrey, First Elden Lord" achievement.
- Defeating **Hoarah Loux, Warrior** at Leyndell, Ashen Capital for the first time unlocks the "Hoarah Loux, Warrior" achievement.
- Godfrey wears the Elden Lord Set (Elden Lord Crown, Elden Lord Armor, Elden Lord Bracers, Elden Lord Greaves).
- Godfrey's lordly posture is maintained by Serosh, whose teeth sink into his left shoulder for the fight. These actions help suppress Godfrey's bloodlust.
 - How Serosh is anchored to Godfrey is similar to how Miquella attaches himself to Promised Consort Radahn. Their entwinement also parallels twin stalks of the Scadutree.
 - Serosh's crown bears an uncanny resemblance to the Elden Lord crown.
- The Axe of Godfrey was unbroken when he gained Serosh and vowed to become a Lord.
 - The axe wielded by the golden phantom version of Godfrey is unbroken and features twin blades, suggesting it represents Godfrey before the Long March.
 - Statues of Godfrey with Serosh and an undamaged axe are found at the Roundtable Hold and in the Stormveil Castle throne room.
 - There is a portrait of Godfrey with a broken axe in Stormveil Castle's main hall, which is guarded by a Grafted Scion. This was likely painted after Godfrey returned to the Lands Between.
 - The Axe of Godfrey strongly resembles the Beastman's Cleavers made by Azula Beastmen.
- Hoarah Loux, Warrior is a highlander.
 - Highlanders are mighty warriors capable of subduing beasts with sheer strength. While most wore blue, only the greatest bear hunters were permitted to wear red. Lord Godfrey is draped in blue, while Hoarah Loux is soaked in red beast blood.
 - The Highland Axe is found directly beneath a large portrait of Godfrey in the main hall of Stormveil. Godfrey’s kinfolk wielded these axes during the Long March.
 - Both Hoarah Loux and the highlanders begin battle by shouting their names.
 - Hoarah Loux roars like a Runebear and Ash of War: Hoarah Loux's Earthshaker is used by Great Red Bears.
 - Just as Godfrey discards the golden lion to become Hoarah Loux, a nameless Redmane forsook the red lion to become Red Bear. Both cover themselves in red after besting savage beasts with their bare hands.
 - The Brave's Battlewear, once the traditional garb of Godfrey's kin, was later repurposed into the Gloried Attire.
- Nepheli Loux, Warrior shares the surname "Loux" with Hoarah Loux, implying a familial or clan relationship.
 - If her questline is completed in her favor, Nepheli may be summoned as a cooperator against Godfrey and Serosh.
 - Although her exact relation is unclear, her age and warrior culture likely make her Godfrey's daughter or a close descendant born after he reverted to Hoarah Loux. Her relationship with Sir Gideon Ofnir may indicate that Godfrey was recalled to the Lands Between when she was young.
 - Godfrey became the lord of Stormveil Castle after defeating the Storm Lord in single combat, establishing the Golden Lineage as the rightful rulers of Limgrave. After the Stormhawk King bonds with Nepheli, Kenneth Haight recognizes her as part of Hoarah Loux’s bloodline, and declares Nepheli the rightful heir to Limgrave.
 - Nepheli Loux claims she swore an oath when she became a warrior. Godfrey also made a vow upon becoming Elden Lord.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Godfrey has a wide range of dialogue lines that cut from the game. At one point, he would have directed the player to cross the Sea of Fog to reclaim the Elden Ring.
- Godfrey had a few differences in .
 - He had two health bars.
 - He delivered an extra line upon defeating the player in phase one: *"Tarnished Warrior. 'Twas nobly fought. Thy rest is well deserved."*
 - Upon death, Hoarah Loux laughed heartily after saying, *"Brave Tarnished. Thy strength befits a crown."*
- Much of Godfrey's character shares ties with the mythical Greek hero, Heracles. Godfrey possesses earthshattering strength, endured harsh trials to earn his godhood, slew the mightiest of the Giants, has a connection with lions through Serosh, and he even enters a berserker state.
- There are also parallels between Godfrey and Arthur, the legendary King of Britain, with both being great warriors once presiding over a lost golden age, and with Arthur himself being away - but prophesied to one day return, reclaim his rule and save his people. Other parallels include the round table seen at the Roundtable Hold, and his chief Crucible Knights, Ordovis and Siluria, being named for ancient Celtic tribes in Pre-Roman Britain.

sections.markdown: is a Boss in Elden Ring. He is a Demigod and a Shardbearer encountered in Stormveil Castle.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Godrick is a descendant of the Golden Lineage, the bloodline that began with Queen Marika the Eternal and her first consort Godfrey. Only a distant relation of Marika's line, his divine blood was sorely diluted, and he was viewed as the runt of the litter. Godrick idolized the first Elden Lord, desiring his ancestor to witness his feats. He wielded an axe emblazoned with a lion, a symbol of Godfrey, and furnished his army with the Erdtree and Serosh emblems of the Golden Lineage. Though he styled himself “lord of all that is golden,” he commanded far less respect than his forebear and was despised by many of his own servants.

After the Elden Ring was shattered, Godrick inherited the Great Rune from the center of the Elden Ring, referred to as the anchor ring. During The Shattering, he was hounded from Leyndell, Royal Capital. He claimed a multitude of treasures, including the Mimic's Veil, and hid among the womenfolk to flee the city. Godrick made his way south, settling in Limgrave with an army of soldiers who had fled Leyndell. He took up residence in Stormveil Castle, using it as a refuge to hide from General Radahn. When Malenia marched southward, Godrick insulted her, leading to a confrontation that left him beaten and humiliated, forced to beg for mercy.

Godrick again retreated to Stormveil Castle to practice grafting, the forbidden art of attaching the parts of other beings to oneself to gain power. When the Tarnished returned to the Lands Between, Godrick sent his soldiers on Tarnished hunts, seeking new subjects to graft. He also produced Grafted Scions; abhorrent beings comprised of many different limbs, seemingly grafted onto children.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.markdown:
The Tarnished journeys to Stormveil Castle in search of Godrick's Great Rune, on the advice of White Mask Varré and Melina. The castle shows many examples of his grafting: severed limbs hanging in the dining hall, a dismembered Troll over a courtyard, and piles of corpses, including the companions of Roderika. Eventually the Tarnished finds Godrick in a graveyard, addressing a dead dragon impaled on a statue. He grafts the dragon's head to his own arm mid-fight, but is defeated, and his Great Rune is claimed.

Later, Nepheli Loux can become the lord of Limgrave at the appointment of Kenneth Haight.

sections.markdown: The **HUD** (heads-up display) in Elden Ring displays several pieces of information, listed below. When the HUD display setting is set to Auto, the HUD will automatically be hidden, except for the compass. Press the [△/Y] button to temporarily display and check the HUD.

sections.heading: HP Gauge
sections.markdown:
Current HP (life force). It decreases as you take damage, and you die when it reaches 0.

HP can regenerate by resting at a Site of Grace, using the Flask of Crimson Tears, or reading incantations.

sections.heading: FP Gauge
sections.markdown:
The power to stay focused in order to use skills and sorcery. It decreases as you use skills and sorcery, and it becomes ineffective when it reaches zero.

FP can regenerate by resting at a Site of Grace or using the Flask of Cerulean Tears.

sections.heading: Stamina Gauge
sections.markdown: This is your current stamina. When it reaches zero, you won’t be able to perform any further actions that consume stamina. Stamina automatically regenerates as time passes. Stamina is not consumed while in a non-combat state.

sections.heading: Status Icons
sections.markdown: When a special effect is active, such as an ability boost, the corresponding status icon will be displayed.

sections.heading: Compass
sections.markdown: Displays the direction. The location of runes that are dropped when you die and landmarks will also be displayed.

sections.heading: Enemy HP
sections.markdown: The enemy’s HP (life force).

sections.heading: Lock-on Marker
sections.markdown: Press the [R3/R] button to lock onto a nearby enemy as a target. You can change targets using the right stick.

sections.heading: Currently Available Skills
sections.markdown: This displays the currently available skills.

sections.heading: Equipment Slot
sections.markdown: The icon of the currently equipped weapon, sorcery, or item will be displayed.

sections.heading: Currently Selected Sorcery
sections.markdown: This is the currently selected sorcery. It cannot be used unless a catalyst has been equipped.

sections.heading: Currently Selected Left-Hand Weapon
sections.markdown: This is the weapon that is currently equipped in the left hand.

sections.heading: Currently Selected Item
sections.markdown: This is the currently selected item and the next item to be displayed.

sections.heading: Currently Selected Right-Hand Weapon

sections.heading: Action Dialog

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Duelists are muscular warriors lightly accoutered in bronze armor adorned with serpent effigies, which represent a traitor to the Erdtree. Whether armed with a Duelist Greataxe and iron ball or twin Battle Hammers, they are unrelenting fighters blessed with boundless stamina.

During the time of Lord Godfrey, these champions honored the Erdtree by participating in gladiatorial combat at colosseums. Their excited spectators were delighted to see the serpents on their armor get battered and broken. However, the gladiators were banished when the colosseums closed during the age of Lord Radagon. While many of them served as Erdtree Burial grave wardens in the catacombs, others became rampaging Mad Pumpkin Heads. Some Grave Warden Duelists now fester with the baleful scarlet rot.

sections.heading: Grave Warden Duelist (Greataxe)
sections.markdown:
These Grave Warden Duelists wield colossal Duelist Greataxes. A chain dangles from the greataxe’s pommel, terminating in a solid iron sphere.

The shadowy Grave Warden Duelist in the Sainted Hero's Grave is immune to damage until it is lured into a circle of holy light, marked by an Erdtree Burial spell sigil.

sections.heading: Grave Warden Duelist (Battle Hammer)

sections.heading: Putrid Grave Warden Duelist (Greataxe)
sections.markdown: These axe-wielding Duelists have been corrupted by Scarlet Rot, which has stained their armor red. Their helms are crowned with many snakes, and when they grab a foe the bronze snake coiled around their arms will come alive and bite them, inflicting Scarlet Rot. One can be found in the Consecrated Snowfield to the north of Ordina, Liturgical Town.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Leans more towards the various Dexterity- and Arcane-scaling affinities.
 - Pairs well with the similarly Dex/Arc-leaning Reduvia as an off-hand weapon for dual wielding.
 - Pairs well with the extra status build-up from Cold and Occult affinities: the former for the added Frostbite build-up and the latter for the added scaling to the Blood Loss build-up.
 - Its Keen affinity actually gives it slightly weaker Dexterity-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Keen, Quality, Lightning, or Cold affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Beast's Roar, Storm Blade, Thunderbolt, and Hoarfrost Stomp (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Keen).
- The innate Blood Loss build-up scales with any Arcane-scaling granted by affinities (Poison, Blood, and Occult).
 - While the Blood affinity grants the exact same amount of build-up and scaling as with any other dagger, it does cause the Blood Loss procs to deal an extra 100 flat damage.
- Curiously, the Strength-scaling of the Keen affinity is actually stronger than that of the Standard affinity, despite the Keen affinity usually greatly decreasing the Strength-scaling of the weapon.
- On the shorter side of daggers.

 - Magic negation receives the secondary 15% negation bonus on Sacred and Cold affinities, Fire negation gets the increase on Lightning affinity, Lightning negation gets the increase on Fire and Flame Art affinities, and Holy negation gets the increase on Magic affinity.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage.

sections.markdown:
- Enhances Golden Order Fundamentalist incantations by 10%.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Only the Faith portion of its scaling applies to Healing and Weapon Buff incantations, most notably making it rather unsuitable for casting Order's Blade.
 - The strongest faith scaling of the hybrid seals at 159%, though that is barely over half of the faith only seals (averaging 250%).
- Incantations boosted by 10% when this seal is held in an active hand (not necessarily cast through) is Discus of Light, Triple Rings of Light, and Radagon's Rings of Light. Most notably, Law of Causality and Order's Blade is not boosted.

- Scales best with an equal split of Intelligence and Faith.

 - A 45/17 or 17/45 split (reaching one middle softcap) gives 244 Incantation Scaling.
 - A 80/17 or 17/80 split (reaching one of the highest softcaps) gives 270 Incantation Scaling.
 - A 45/45 split (reaching both middle softcaps) gives 338 Incantation Scaling, comparable to an Erdtree Seal gaining 353 Incantation Scaling at 80 Faith.
- For casting Incantations with a faith requirement below 17, the Frenzied Flame Seal is potentially better due to much lower Attribute requirements (none at all) but is attainable only later, and requires completing Lightseeker Hyetta's questline and at least partially committing to her Ending.

 Sleep is highly effective against both enemies and temporarily incapacitates them when inflicted. Recusant Bernahl is available as a summon for this boss.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **God-Devouring Serpent**, also known as the **elder serpent**, **great serpent**, and **Serpent King**, is an optional Demigod boss in Elden Ring. The God-Devouring Serpent is the first phase of the fight against Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy. Defeating this boss triggers a cutscene that initiates the battle with Rykard. It must be defeated to advance Tanith's questline.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown: The great serpent is an enormous blue snake with arms and an affinity for both lava sorceries and poison. This boss is weak to the Serpent-Hunter's Great-Serpent Hunt, the true power of which activates during this encounter.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Hated for its tremendous and insatiable gluttony, the elder serpent of Mt. Gelmir is an immortal terror that seeks to one day consume the entire world. It has been repelled by the white light of the Serpent-Hunter since ancient times. A cult on Mt. Gelmir practiced hexes and performed human sacrifices in reverence to a heretical serpent god. Over time, these practices ceased, and their Gelmir Sorcery was lost.

During the reign of Queen Marika, it was rediscovered by the Demigod Rykard. During the Shattering, Praetor Rykard willingly allowed the great serpent to devour him. Although his Gelmir Knights obtained the legendary Serpent-Hunter weapon, they failed to defeat their former lord. Now, the great serpent and Rykard share a single body as the Lord of Blasphemy, engaging in an appalling birthing ritual that spawned the Man-Serpents. They devour countless champions with the ultimate goal of consuming the gods and the world itself.

sections.heading: Location
sections.markdown: The God-Devouring Serpent can be found at the Volcano Manor on Mt. Gelmir, near the Audience Pathway site of grace.

sections.heading: Combat Overview
sections.markdown:
- HP: **30,739**
- Defense: **?**
- Stance: **?**
- Deals Standard and Fire damage, and inflicts Poison buildup.
- Weakness: Serpent-Hunter
- Vulnerable to Frostbite.
- Cannot be Parried.
- Can be Stance-broken, but is not vulnerable to a Critical Attack.
- Defeating this boss triggers a cutscene and the battle against Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- If the player defeats the God-Devouring Serpent but is killed by Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, then they must defeat the God-Devouring Serpent again.
- The Blasphemous Blade was stored within the mouth of the God-Devouring Serpent.
- The emblem of the Volcano Manor and the sigil for Gelmir Sorceries depict the great serpent consuming Rykard.
- Serpents were viewed as traitors to the Erdtree long before the great serpent devoured Rykard.
It must be defeated to advance Tanith's questline.

- Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy called the God-Devouring Serpent "**Eveligne**" in an unused version of the boss transition cutscene.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Godskin Duo** is a boss battle where you have to battle against a Godskin Apostle and Godskin Noble at the same time. They can be found in Crumbling Farum Azula. This is **not** an optional boss as they must be defeated to advance further in Crumbling Farum Azula.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.markdown:
The Godskin Duo share one health bar of around 24000 HP (NG), but also still have their own HP. If one is killed, it will either respawn automatically after ~15 seconds or the other Godskin will reanimate them. They will also still enter phase 2 if dropping close to 50% in individual HP.

The pillars within the arena are an effective way to separate them, although their phase 2 attacks will demolish the upper portion of them. In addition, both of them can be parried.

Sleep Pots can serve as a way to buy time as both bosses can be rendered temporarily paralyzed by sleep status.

sections.markdown: Part of the Godskin Noble Set, acquired after defeating the Godskin Noble at the Liurnia Tower Bridge.

sections.heading: Trivia

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Gold Bracelets** are Armwear in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown: - The Gold Bracelets are obtained by completing Goldmask's questline.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Slot: Arms
- Part of the Goldmask's Set, which also includes Goldmask's Rags, the Radiant Gold Mask, and the Gold Waistwrap.
- Worn by Goldmask.
- Sell value: 500 runes

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Golden Prosthetic** was Armwear that was cut from Elden Ring. This item is unobtainable.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown: - The playable version of Golden Prosthetic is cut content and cannot be acquired.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Slot: Arms
- Part of Millicent's Set
- Worn by Millicent after she receives the Valkyrie's Prosthesis
- Sell value: 500
- Miquella made Unalloyed Gold prosthetics for Malenia the Severed, who suffered from scarlet rot.

sections.heading: Trivia

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Godskin Apostle Trousers** is an armor piece found in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Description
sections.markdown:
Trousers made by sewing together patches of smooth skin. Worn by the Godskin Apostles.*
The apostles, once said to serve Destined Death, are wielders of the god-slaying black flame. But after their defeat by Maliketh, the Black Blade, the source of their power was sealed away.*

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown: Received alongside with the rest of the set upon defeating the Godskin Apostle boss at the bottom of the Divine Tower of Caelid.
